result.topic_en: Hilbert argues that all sciences that produce lasting results ultimately supply material for mathematics, citing Einstein's 1912 letter to Sommerfeld, and proposes grounding logic in physical-mechanical considerations as an invariant kind of 'happening'; he then begins a thesis on applying the laws of probability to logic and mathematical statements.
